title: Grayscale on the GPU
author: Dimitris Yfantidis
summary: A large photo converted to grayscale by an OpenCL kernel.
description: Loads a 15,000-pixel-wide photo, converts every pixel to grayscale in an OpenCL kernel, prints how long the kernel took and shows the result. Compare it with the CPU version.
how_it_works: The photo is decoded with SDL_image and copied to the OpenCL device. The kernel runs once per pixel: it reads the pixel's four bytes, computes its luminance with the Rec. 709 weights (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B) and writes that to red, green and blue, keeping alpha.
The time printed is the kernel alone, measured with OpenCL profiling events, so copying the image to and from the device is not counted.
highlights: The kernel time in the console (the terminal button at the top), against the CPU version's time.
Every pixel is independent, which is exactly the kind of work GPUs are built for.
Pick another OpenCL device in Settings to compare them.
